profiles.name: Gemini CLI (google-gemini/gemini-cli)
profiles.one_liner: Google's Apache-2.0, TypeScript/Node terminal coding agent for Gemini models, notable for a tiered TOML policy engine, an 11-event vetoing hook system, all-in-one extensions (MCP + commands + hooks + skills + agents + policies), shadow-git checkpointing and a 1M-token context; since June 18, 2026 the free/consumer tiers were moved to the closed-source Go "Antigravity CLI" while the repo continues for enterprise/API-key users.

dimensions.identity: Maintained by Google under the google-gemini GitHub org; announced June 25, 2025 with Gemini 2.5 Pro, a 1M-token context and a free tier of 60 requests/min and 1,000 requests/day. Apache-2.0, written in TypeScript on Node.js >=20 with a React/Ink TUI (packages/cli) over a packages/core engine; shipped as the npm package @google/gemini-cli (bin `gemini`, also Homebrew/MacPorts), plus a library (@google/gemini-cli-sdk exposing GeminiCliAgent), a VS Code companion, an ACP mode for editors, and an experimental a2a-server. Popularity: ~107.2k GitHub stars / 14.6k forks and 364,209 npm downloads in the week of Sep 18-24, 2026. Current stable is v0.61.0 (Sep 23, 2026) on weekly stable/preview plus nightly channels. Status caveat: on May 19, 2026 Google announced that on June 18, 2026 Gemini CLI would "stop serving requests for Google AI Pro and Ultra, as well as those using it free of charge" (migrated to the closed-source, Go-based Antigravity CLI), while "the project remains available to the community as an Apache 2.0 licensed repository with no changes" and keeps receiving model updates, bug and security fixes for enterprise (Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise, Cloud/API-key/Vertex) customers.
dimensions.loop: A single ReAct-style tool-calling loop in packages/core: GeminiClient.sendMessageStream() -> processTurn() -> Turn.run(), an async generator over chat.sendMessageStream() that yields GeminiEventType events (Content, Thought, ToolCallRequest, ToolCallResponse, Citation, Finished, Error, UserCancelled, Retry, ChatCompressed, LoopDetected, MaxSessionTurns, AgentExecutionStopped/Blocked); function calls are collected into pendingToolCalls, executed by the CLI scheduler (READ_ONLY_KINDS may run in parallel, MUTATOR_KINDS gated), and results fed back. The per-request ceiling is `const MAX_TURNS = 100` (bounded via Math.min); model.maxSessionTurns (default -1 = unlimited) is checked before each API call and headless mode exits with code 53 when the turn limit is hit. A turn ends on a finishReason/error/cancel; when the model stops without tool calls, checkNextSpeaker() runs and if it answers next_speaker === 'model' the client sends "Please continue." and recurses with the remaining turn budget. LoopDetectionService hashes tool name+args and trips on 5 identical repeats (TOOL_CALL_LOOP_THRESHOLD, cycles of 1-5 tools), on a 50-char content chunk repeating 10 times, and after 30 turns runs an LLM judge every ~10 turns at 0.9 confidence; a first detection triggers _recoverFromLoop (corrective feedback injected), repeats abort the turn (model.disableLoopDetection to turn off). Plan Mode (enter_plan_mode/exit_plan_mode tools, --approval-mode=plan, Shift+Tab) adds an optional read-only plan-then-execute phase with plans written under ~/.gemini/tmp/<project>/<session-id>/plans/.
dimensions.tools: Tools are TypeScript classes: DeclarativeTool/BaseDeclarativeTool (validateToolParams() returning an error string or null, build() -> a ToolInvocation with getDescription(), shouldConfirmExecute() and execute()), a Kind enum (Read/Edit/Delete/Execute...) split into MUTATOR_KINDS vs READ_ONLY_KINDS, ToolConfirmationOutcome {ProceedOnce, ProceedAlways, ProceedAlwaysAndSave, Cancel}, and a ToolResult carrying `llmContent` (what goes into model history) separately from `returnDisplay` (markdown for the user); BaseToolInvocation routes confirmations through the policy engine via getMessageBusDecision(). Built-ins listed in docs/reference/tools.md: read_file, write_file, replace, list_directory, glob, grep_search (alias search_file_content, ripgrep by default), read_many_files (@ syntax), run_shell_command (params command, description, dir_path, is_background; PTY interactive shell, tools.shell.inactivityTimeout 300 s, subprocess sees GEMINI_CLI=1), web_fetch, google_web_search, ask_user, write_todos, activate_skill, get_internal_docs, enter_plan_mode/exit_plan_mode, and experimental tracker_* task tools; memory is persisted by editing GEMINI.md through write_file/replace. Non-MCP custom tools can be discovered via tools.discoveryCommand and invoked via tools.callCommand (tool name as first arg, JSON args on stdin, JSON result on stdout); tools.core allowlists and tools.exclude blocklists built-ins. Output limits: tools.truncateToolOutputThreshold (default 40000 chars, <=0 disables), contextManagement.tools.distillation.maxOutputTokens 10000 with summarizationThresholdTokens 20000 (outputs above that are LLM-summarized), and model.summarizeToolOutput per-tool tokenBudget (currently only run_shell_command).
dimensions.extensibility: Extensions are directories with a gemini-extension.json manifest (name, version, description, mcpServers using ${extensionPath}/${workspacePath}, contextFileName defaulting to GEMINI.md, excludeTools including command-scoped entries like "run_shell_command(rm -rf)", settings [{name, description, envVar, sensitive}], themes, policies, plan, migratedTo) plus conventional subfolders: commands/*.toml (deploy.toml -> /deploy, gcs/sync.toml -> /gcs:sync), hooks/hooks.json, skills/<name>/SKILL.md, agents/*.md and policies/*.toml. Install/manage with `gemini extensions install <github-url|path> [--ref --auto-update --consent]`, `link <path>` for local dev, `new <path> [mcp-server|context|custom-commands]`, enable/disable --scope, update --all, and a gallery at geminicli.com/extensions; extension policies sit at tier 2 and cannot contain `allow` decisions, sensitive env vars are filtered from extension processes, and admins can gate with admin.extensions.enabled, security.allowedExtensions (regex) and security.blockGitExtensions. Agent Skills follow the open SKILL.md standard with progressive disclosure via the activate_skill tool, discovered from built-in -> extension -> ~/.gemini/skills (or ~/.agents/skills) -> .gemini/skills (or .agents/skills). Pluggable surfaces are therefore tools (MCP or discoveryCommand), prompts/commands, hooks (type "command" only), subagents, skills, policies and themes; model providers and the loop itself are not pluggable, and a programmatic route exists through @google/gemini-cli-sdk.
dimensions.context: Instruction memory is hierarchical GEMINI.md: ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md, then project root and ancestors (stopping at context.memoryBoundaryMarkers, default [".git"], scanning up to context.discoveryMaxDirs 200), then just-in-time loading of GEMINI.md files in directories a tool touches; all are concatenated into every prompt, context.fileName accepts a list such as ["AGENTS.md","CONTEXT.md","GEMINI.md"], @./file.md imports (memport) split large files, and /memory show|list|reload inspect it; saying "remember that..." makes the agent edit the appropriate GEMINI.md, and experimental.autoMemory (default false) extracts skills in the background. Compression is automatic or via /compress: model.compressionThreshold (default 0.5, lowered from the older COMPRESSION_TOKEN_THRESHOLD 0.7 in PR #13517, Nov 20, 2025) triggers a summarizer that rewrites history as an XML state_snapshot (overall_goal, key_knowledge, file_system_state, current_plan), and a newer contextManagement block sets historyWindow.maxTokens 150000, historyWindow.retainedTokens 40000, messageLimits.normalMaxTokens 2500 and retainedMaxTokens 12000. Sessions persist with --resume/-r, /resume save|resume, --list-sessions, general.sessionRetention.maxAge (default 30d); general.checkpointing.enabled snapshots the tree into a shadow git repo at ~/.gemini/history/<project_hash> plus a JSON checkpoint in ~/.gemini/tmp/<project_hash>/checkpoints before every approved file-modifying tool, restorable with /restore, while /rewind (Esc twice) reverts chat and/or code. KV/prefix caching: implicit token caching applies only to API-key and Vertex auth (Code Assist OAuth "does not support cached content creation"), with savings shown by /stats.
dimensions.permissions: Approval modes form a permissiveness ladder plan < default < auto_edit < yolo (general.defaultApprovalMode, --approval-mode, Shift+Tab; --yolo auto-approves and enables the sandbox; security.disableYoloMode and security.disableAlwaysAllow let admins remove the escape hatches). Fine-grained gating goes through the policy engine: TOML rules in ~/.gemini/policies/*.toml (user) and /etc/gemini-cli/policies (admin; workspace tier currently disabled) with fields toolName (wildcards, mcp_*), decision allow|deny|ask_user, priority 0-999, argsPattern regex over JSON args, commandPrefix/commandRegex, mcpName, subagent, modes, interactive, allowRedirection and denyMessage; precedence is final_priority = tier_base + priority/1000 with tiers default 1, extension 2, workspace 3, user 4, admin 5, defaults allow read-only tools and ask_user for writers/shell, and /policies lists active rules. Shell allowlisting uses tools.allowed / tools.core entries like "run_shell_command(git)", commands chained with &&, || or ; are split and each segment validated, and tools.exclude wins over any allow. Sandboxing via -s/--sandbox, GEMINI_SANDBOX=docker|podman|sandbox-exec|runsc|lxc or tools.sandbox: six macOS Seatbelt profiles (permissive-open default, permissive-proxied, restrictive-open/proxied, strict-open/proxied via SEATBELT_PROFILE), the gemini-cli-sandbox Docker image or a project .gemini/sandbox.Dockerfile, gVisor runsc, experimental LXC, plus tools.sandboxAllowedPaths / sandboxNetworkAccess and per-tool security.toolSandboxing. Folder trust (security.folderTrust.enabled, ~/.gemini/trustedFolders.json, /permissions) disables project settings, .env, hooks, MCP servers, extensions and auto-accept in untrusted directories, and security.enableConseca (default false) adds an LLM that generates and enforces per-prompt security policies; the CVSS 10.0 CVE-2026-12537 (Apr 24, 2026, fixed in 0.39.1) came from headless mode auto-trusting workspaces and --yolo ignoring the tool allowlist.
dimensions.hooks: Hooks are configured under "hooks" in settings.json (project .gemini/settings.json > ~/.gemini/settings.json > /etc/gemini-cli/settings.json) or in an extension's hooks/hooks.json, and fire on 11 events: SessionStart, SessionEnd, BeforeAgent, AfterAgent, BeforeModel, AfterModel, BeforeToolSelection, BeforeTool, AfterTool, PreCompress and Notification. Each entry has a matcher (regex for tool events, e.g. "write_file|replace"; exact string for lifecycle events; "*" for all) and a list of hooks with type "command" (the only type), command, optional name/description and timeout (default 60000 ms). The hook receives the event JSON on stdin and must print only a JSON object on stdout such as {"decision":"allow"|"deny","message":"...","modifications":{}}; exit 0 means parse the JSON, exit 2 is a hard system block whose stderr becomes the rejection reason, other codes are non-fatal warnings. Hooks can veto: BeforeTool blocks a tool call, BeforeAgent rejects a prompt, BeforeModel blocks or mocks the LLM call, AfterModel redacts output, AfterTool hides a result, BeforeToolSelection filters the tool list, AfterAgent can retry or halt, while SessionEnd and PreCompress are advisory. Hooks run with GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR, GEMINI_SESSION_ID, GEMINI_CWD, GEMINI_PLANS_DIR (and a CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR alias), are fingerprinted so changed commands trigger a warning, are disabled in untrusted folders, and are managed with /hooks.
dimensions.subagents: Subagents are Markdown files with YAML frontmatter in .gemini/agents/*.md (project) or ~/.gemini/agents/*.md (user), with fields name, description, kind local|remote, tools (list with wildcards * and mcp_*), model (defaults to the session model), temperature (default 1), max_turns (default 30), timeout_mins (default 10) and an isolated mcpServers block. The parent sees each subagent as a tool and delegates automatically, or the user forces it with an @name prefix (e.g. @codebase_investigator); each child runs its own isolated conversation loop and tool registry, inherits all parent tools if `tools` is omitted, and cannot invoke other subagents (no recursion, so depth is 1). Policy rules can target a child via the `subagent` field, agents.overrides tunes maxTurns/timeout per agent, experimental.enableAgents (default true) toggles the feature, and /agents lists/enables/disables them. Built-ins are codebase_investigator, cli_help, generalist (inherits everything) and browser_agent (Chrome 144+); on completion the child returns a findings report that the parent folds into its history. kind: remote subagents speak A2A (agent_card_url or agent_card_json; auth apiKey, http, google-credentials restricted to *.googleapis.com/*.run.app, or OAuth PKCE; 2 retries), and experimental.worktrees adds git-worktree automation.
dimensions.providers: Gemini only, through the @google/genai SDK: Google OAuth via the Code Assist API (free/AI Pro/Ultra access ended June 18, 2026; Code Assist Standard/Enterprise licenses continue), GEMINI_API_KEY from AI Studio, Vertex AI (gcloud ADC, service-account JSON, or GOOGLE_API_KEY + GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT), and automatic Cloud Shell/GCE metadata credentials; GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL / GOOGLE_VERTEX_BASE_URL (HTTPS) allow a proxy, which the community uses with LiteLLM to front Ollama, but that is unofficial. Local models are supported only as a router: experimental.gemmaModelRouter (enabled, classifier.host e.g. http://localhost:9379, classifier.model) runs gemma3-1b-gpu-custom (~968 MB) on LiteRT-LM via `gemini gemma setup` to decide which hosted model answers, never to answer itself; a Mar 29, 2026 discussion (#24166) requesting Ollama/OpenAI-compatible providers has no maintainer reply. Model selection precedence is --model > GEMINI_MODEL > model.name > default "auto", with ModelAvailabilityService prompting the user to fall back on failures and a silent fallback chain (flash-lite -> flash -> pro) for internal utility calls; modelConfigs.aliases/modelDefinitions/modelChains define fallback policies (terminal, transient, not_found, unknown). Handling of weak models is not documented beyond routing, fallback and loop recovery.
dimensions.mcp: Gemini CLI is an MCP client (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.23) supporting stdio (command, args, env with $VAR expansion, cwd), SSE (url) and streamable HTTP (httpUrl, headers) servers configured under mcpServers with timeout (default 600000 ms), trust (skip confirmations), includeTools/excludeTools (exclude wins), and OAuth 2.0 with dynamic discovery, Google credentials or service-account impersonation (targetAudience/targetServiceAccount), validating the RFC 9207 iss parameter. MCP tools are namespaced mcp_{server}_{tool} (sanitized, truncated at 63 chars; avoid underscores in server names because the policy parser splits on the first underscore), MCP prompts become slash commands (/poem-writer --title=...), resources are embedded with @server://path, and CallToolResult content arrays with images/audio are passed to the model; /mcp list|auth|enable|disable and `gemini mcp add|list|remove` manage servers, and admin.mcp.enabled/config/requiredConfig lock them down. Acting as an MCP server is not documented. Other standards: `gemini --acp` runs it as an Agent Client Protocol agent (@agentclientprotocol/sdk 0.16.1; it was Zed's reference ACP agent and is in the ACP registry for JetBrains), remote subagents and the experimental packages/a2a-server use Google's A2A protocol, and the VS Code companion injects active-file/cursor/selection deltas into the loop.
dimensions.evals: Google publishes no benchmark for the CLI harness itself: the June 25, 2025 launch post makes no benchmark claims, the v0.61.0 changelog (Sep 23, 2026) is all security/reliability fixes, and the repo documents integration tests but no eval suite or harness-vs-model ablation. Third-party coverage confirms the gap: a Sep 26, 2026 CodeAnt comparison states "Google publishes no Terminal-Bench figure for the CLI harness" and notes Gemini CLI is absent from Terminus-2, and the Sep 2026 Terminal-Bench 4.0 write-ups list no Gemini CLI row, only model-level Gemini entries (Gemini 3.8 Flash 87.6% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 versus 19.1-19.7% on 4.0 run through mini-SWE-agent / Artificial Analysis harnesses) and Gemini 3.1 Pro at 80.6% on SWE-bench Verified. The only harness-level numbers are anecdotal, e.g. a June 2026 review's Express.js task taking 47 minutes longer than Claude Code with three manual corrections. Not documented by the project.
dimensions.distinctive: Distinctive ideas: (1) a declarative, tiered TOML policy engine (final_priority = tier_base + priority/1000 across default/extension/workspace/user/admin) that unifies approval modes, per-tool argsPattern rules, MCP and subagent scoping, extension-shipped policies and optional LLM-generated Conseca policies into one decision path; (2) the broadest lifecycle-hook surface among the CLIs, 11 events including BeforeModel/AfterModel/BeforeToolSelection with JSON veto/modification, paired with an all-in-one extension package (MCP servers + commands + hooks + skills + agents + policies + themes in a single gemini-extension.json); (3) Google-native context engineering: a 1M-token window, a google_web_search grounding tool, shadow-git checkpointing with /restore, JIT GEMINI.md loading and a local 1B Gemma model used purely as a routing classifier. Loudest criticisms: agentic-loop quality (users report proposing the same fix repeatedly, 15-minute hangs, unrequested large refactors, and a PowerShell-based edit corrupting file comments, discussion #24725, Apr 2026); the CVSS 10.0 CVE-2026-12537 RCE via headless auto-trust and --yolo allowlist bypass (Apr 2026); provider lock-in with no Ollama/OpenAI-compatible support; and the June 18, 2026 transition that moved free/Pro/Ultra users to the closed-source Go Antigravity CLI (reported 20 free requests/day versus 1,000), which the community reads as an open-source project being wound down into a proprietary product.

unknowns: evals: no harness-level benchmark or harness-vs-model ablation is published by the project; only third-party model-level numbers exist
providers: handling of weak/small models is not documented beyond model routing, fallback chains and loop recovery
mcp: whether Gemini CLI can itself act as an MCP server is not documented

context: the current COMPRESSION_PRESERVE_THRESHOLD (fraction of recent history kept uncompressed) could not be confirmed from current source; only the older 0.7 trigger / last-30% behavior is documented in issue #12068
identity: the Antigravity CLI free quota (20 requests/day) comes from secondary reporting, not the official announcement, which gives no quota figures
permissions: workspace-tier policies are documented as disabled due to a known issue, so project-level TOML rules cannot be relied on
tools: per-tool truncation for read_file/grep beyond the global truncateToolOutputThreshold and distillation settings is not documented

profiles.name: Aider (Aider-AI/aider)
profiles.one_liner: Open-source, git-first terminal pair programmer (Python, Apache-2.0) built on plain-text edit formats and a PageRank repo map rather than tool calling; still widely installed in 2026 but effectively in maintenance mode, with the cecli/aider-ce fork carrying the agent-mode and MCP work.

dimensions.identity: Maintained by Paul Gauthier under the Aider-AI GitHub org; repo created 2023-05-09 and the oldest PyPI release visible is aider-chat v0.5.0 on 2023-06-08. Apache-2.0, pure Python (requires Python >=3.10,<3.13), shipped as a CLI (`pip install aider-install; aider-install`, or `aider-chat` on PyPI), with an optional Streamlit web UI (`--gui`/`--browser`), official Docker images `paulgauthier/aider` and `paulgauthier/aider-full`, and an explicitly unsupported Python API (`from aider.coders import Coder; Coder.create(main_model=..., fnames=...).run(...)`). GitHub API on 2026-09-26: 49,199 stars, 4,995 forks, 1,897 open issues, last push 2026-05-22; the README claims 6.8M PyPI installs, 15B tokens/week, and a top-20 OpenRouter app ranking. Latest PyPI version is 0.86.2 (2026-02-12); the last tagged GitHub release is v0.86.1 (Aug 2025), and the `main` branch has since only added model settings (Claude 4.5/4.6/4.7, GPT-5.1–5.4, Gemini 3 previews) plus an `/ok` shortcut.
dimensions.loop: Aider is deliberately 'interactive, not agentic': one user message produces one LLM response, which is parsed for edit blocks and applied, then the turn ends. The only autonomy is the reflection loop in `Coder.run_one()` (aider/coders/base_coder.py): `max_reflections = 3`, and a reflection is re-sent to the model when (a) the reply mentions files not yet in chat and the user agrees to add them, (b) `--auto-lint` reports errors, (c) `--auto-test` fails, or (d) an edit block is malformed (the failure text is fed back). The loop is `while message: self.reflected_message = None; send_message(message); if not self.reflected_message: break`, with a warning 'Only 3 reflections allowed, stopping.' Architect mode (`--architect`) is a fixed two-call planner/executor: the main model writes a free-form plan, then an editor model (`--editor-model`, default derived from the main model) turns it into edits using `editor-diff`/`editor-whole` prompts; `--auto-accept-architect` defaults to True. `/context` mode (v0.79.0, `context_coder.py`) is a mini-loop that asks the model which files need editing and reflects until the mentioned set matches, capped at `max_reflections - 1`. There is no tool-call loop, no step budget beyond the 3 reflections, and no background execution.
dimensions.tools: Aider has no tool/function-calling registry: the model returns prose plus text edit blocks that a Coder subclass parses. The 'tool set' is therefore the set of edit formats, each a class in aider/coders/ (`editblock_coder.py` = `diff` with `<<<<<<< SEARCH`/`=======`/`>>>>>>> REPLACE` markers, `editblock_fenced_coder.py` = `diff-fenced` for Gemini, `udiff_coder.py`/`udiff_simple.py`, `wholefile_coder.py` = `whole`, `patch_coder.py` for GPT-4.1, `editor_*_coder.py` for architect mode, plus `ask_coder.py`, `help_coder.py`, `context_coder.py`, `architect_coder.py`; `*_func_coder.py` variants exist in the tree but no shipped default uses function calling). Side effects are limited to: writing files, creating new files (`fname.touch()` when a SEARCH block is empty), git commits, and shell commands the model emits in ```bash/```sh fences, which `run_shell_commands()` only runs after `io.confirm_ask(..., explicit_yes_required=True, allow_never=True)`. Failed SEARCH/REPLACE blocks are reported back verbatim: '# SearchReplaceNoExactMatch: This SEARCH block failed to exactly match', 'Did you mean to match some of these actual lines', '# N SEARCH/REPLACE blocks failed', 'The other N were applied successfully. Don't re-send them.' Lint/test output is returned as the reflected message; shell output is added to the chat only if the user confirms; there is no documented truncation limit for tool output (the model's context window is the only bound).
dimensions.extensibility: There is no plugin system. What is configurable: models via `.aider.model.settings.yml` (fields `name`, `edit_format`, `weak_model_name`, `editor_model_name`, `editor_edit_format`, `use_repo_map`, `lazy`, `overeager`, `reminder`, `examples_as_sys_msg`, `cache_control`, `use_temperature`, `streaming`, `reasoning_tag`, `remove_reasoning`, `system_prompt_prefix`, `accepts_settings`, and `extra_params` passed straight to `litellm.completion()`, with the special name `aider/extra_params` applying to all models) and `.aider.model.metadata.json` (`max_input_tokens`, `max_output_tokens`, costs); prompts via `--read CONVENTIONS.md`; external commands via `--lint-cmd 'lang: cmd'`, `--test-cmd`, `--notifications-command`; startup command scripts via `--load`; all flags mirrored as `AIDER_*` env vars and `.aider.conf.yml`. Adding a new edit format or provider means subclassing `Coder`/editing `aider/coders/` and `aider/models.py` in a fork. The Python API is documented as 'not officially supported... could change without backwards compatibility'. The cecli/aider-ce fork's roadmap adds what upstream lacks (a hooks base class for user-defined Python hooks, agent tools, MCP).
dimensions.context: Context is managed by three mechanisms. (1) The repo map (`aider/repomap.py`): tree-sitter (via tree-sitter-language-pack) extracts definitions/references, cached in `.aider.tags.cache.v4` with diskcache; a networkx `MultiDiGraph` gets edges from referencing file to defining file with weights (10x for identifiers mentioned in chat or long camelCase/snake_case names, 0.1x for `_private` or identifiers defined in 5+ files, 50x when the referencer is a chat file), `nx.pagerank(G, weight='weight', personalization=...)` ranks files, and a binary search over the ranked tag list fits `--map-tokens` (default 1024) within a 15% tolerance; with no files in chat the budget is multiplied by `--map-multiplier-no-files` (CLI default 2); `--map-refresh auto|always|files|manual` (auto re-caches only when map build exceeds 1s). (2) Chat history: `ChatSummary` summarises `done_messages` with the weak model when `too_big()`, using `max_chat_history_tokens = min(max(max_input_tokens/16, 1024), 8192)` (overridable with `--max-chat-history-tokens`); `/clear`, `/tokens`, `/drop` are manual. (3) Memory files: there is no CLAUDE.md-style auto-loaded file; the convention is `--read CONVENTIONS.md` or `read: [CONVENTIONS.md]` in `.aider.conf.yml`, which marks it read-only and cacheable. Prompt ordering is cache-friendly by design (`chat_chunks.py`): system prompt, read-only files, repo map, then editable files and current message; `--cache-prompts` adds cache_control markers for Anthropic and DeepSeek and `--cache-keepalive-pings N` sends up to N pings at 5-minute intervals to keep Anthropic's cache warm. Persistence across sessions is only `.aider.chat.history.md`/`.aider.input.history` in the repo.
dimensions.permissions: There are no permission modes, allow/deny rules, or sandbox. Every side effect is an interactive `confirm_ask` (add a file the model mentioned, create a file, run a suggested shell command, scrape a URL with `--detect-urls`, apply lint fixes), with 'don't ask again' groups (`allow_never`) and `--yes-always` to accept everything (which is how the SWE-bench and polyglot harnesses run it). Shell commands require an explicit yes (`explicit_yes_required=True`) and can be disabled entirely with `--no-suggest-shell-commands`; `/run` and `/test` execute whatever the user types. Edits are fenced only by convention: the model may only edit files the user has `/add`ed, the repo map and `/read-only` files are labelled read-only in the prompt, `.aiderignore` and `--subtree-only` hide parts of a monorepo, and `--no-gitignore`/`--add-gitignore-files` control gitignored files; nothing enforces the fence at the OS level. The recommended isolation is running the `paulgauthier/aider` Docker image with `--volume $(pwd):/app`, which the docs present as a deployment option (noting `/run` then executes inside the container), not as a security boundary. Git is the real safety net: `--auto-commits` (default on) commits every edit and `--dirty-commits` commits your pending work first, so `/undo` reverts one aider change.
dimensions.hooks: not documented — Aider has no lifecycle hook or event system. The nearest fixed equivalents are post-edit actions: `--auto-lint` (default on, built-in tree-sitter linters or `--lint-cmd`), `--auto-test` with `--test-cmd` (default off), and `--notifications`/`--notifications-command` fired when a response is ready; each feeds failures back into the reflection loop but none can veto an edit before it lands. Git pre-commit hooks are skipped by default (`--git-commit-verify` re-enables them). `--load FILE` runs slash commands at startup. The cecli fork's roadmap lists 'hooks base class for user defined python hooks with an execute method with type and priority settings' as future work, confirming upstream has none.
dimensions.subagents: not documented — Aider has no sub-agent or multi-agent facility. The closest structures are model roles inside one turn: the architect/editor split (main model plans, `--editor-model` edits using an `editor-*` format, `--auto-accept-architect` defaults True) and the `--weak-model` used for commit messages and history summarisation; both are fixed two-call pipelines with no separate context, tools, or permissions, and the editor's output returns to the same chat. Parallelism is left to the user (run several aider processes; the SWE-bench harness simply retried from scratch with alternate models). The cecli/aider-ce fork advertises subagents with distinct MCP server sets and a planned `/invoke-agent` command with 'their own context and workspaces', but that is not upstream.
dimensions.providers: Fully provider-agnostic through litellm: docs list 18+ providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, xAI, Azure, Bedrock, Vertex, Cohere, Groq, DeepSeek, OpenRouter with OAuth, GitHub Copilot) plus any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (`--openai-api-base`, `--api-key PROVIDER=KEY`, `--set-env`). Local models are first-class: Ollama (`OLLAMA_API_BASE`, `ollama_chat/<model>` recommended over `ollama/`, and since v0.74 aider sets `num_ctx = int(token_count(messages) * 1.25) + 8192` per request because Ollama defaults to a 2k window and 'silently discards context'), LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM via the OpenAI-compatible path; a fixed window is set with `extra_params: {num_ctx: 65536}` in `.aider.model.settings.yml`. Weak-model handling is explicit: unknown models default to `edit_format: whole` and `use_repo_map: False`; per-model `lazy` ('You are diligent and tireless! You NEVER leave comments describing code without implementing it!') and `overeager` ('Do what they ask, but no more.') prompt flags; `--edit-format whole` or `--architect` are the documented fallbacks for models that cannot produce SEARCH/REPLACE blocks; and the docs warn 'models weaker than GPT 3.5 may have problems' and that above ~25k tokens 'most models start to become distracted'. Reasoning models get `--reasoning-effort`, `--thinking-tokens`, `reasoning_tag`/`remove_reasoning`, and 'infinite output' continuation via assistant prefill on Anthropic/DeepSeek/Mistral/Bedrock/Vertex models.
dimensions.mcp: No native MCP client or server, and no ACP/A2A support. The options reference has no MCP flag; community requests (#2525, #3314, and RFC #4506 'Add native MCP server and Agent Mode support to Aider CLI', opened 2025-09-09) remain open with no maintainer response, and the exploratory PR #3937 was closed unmerged. Integration is only by wrapping: third-party 'aider-mcp-server' projects (danielscholl, sengokudaikon) expose aider as an MCP tool to Claude Desktop/Cursor, the AiderDesk GUI adds MCP and an agent mode on top of aider, and the cecli/aider-ce fork ships an agent mode with MCP server configuration (transport/url/command) and per-agent MCP sets. Inside upstream aider the only external-context tools are `/web <url>` (Playwright scraping), `/run`, and `/read-only`.
dimensions.evals: Aider publishes its own benchmarks and leaderboards (aider.chat/docs/leaderboards/). The current one is the polyglot benchmark (Dec 2024): 225 of the hardest Exercism exercises across C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, Rust (selected as those solved by 3 or fewer of 7 models), scored as `pass_rate_2` (second attempt after test failures are fed back) with `percent_cases_well_formed` measuring edit-format compliance and cost per run. The leaderboard YAML has 60 entries, the newest dated 2025-10-03 (DeepSeek-V3.2 Reasoner 74.2%, $1.30) and none from 2026; top rows are gpt-5 (high) 88.0%/$29.08 diff, gpt-5 (medium) 86.7%, o3-pro (high) 84.9%/$146.32, gemini-2.5-pro 83.1% diff-fenced, and o3 (high)+gpt-4.1 architect 78.2%. Older harness ablations are its most useful evidence: the 89-task refactoring benchmark showed GPT-4 Turbo going from 20% (SEARCH/REPLACE, 12 lazy tasks) to 61% (udiff, 4 lazy tasks); the architect/editor post showed Sonnet+Sonnet 80.5% vs 77.4% solo and o1-preview+Sonnet 82.7%. External: 26.3% on SWE-bench Lite (May 2024, six alternating GPT-4o/Opus attempts with lint+test plausibility checks; 20.3% on the first GPT-4o attempt alone) and 18.9% on full SWE-bench (June 2024). Aider is not on Terminal-Bench or 2026 SWE-bench Verified leaderboards, and no 2026 self-published scores exist.
dimensions.distinctive: Three ideas are genuinely its own: (1) the tree-sitter + PageRank repo map that spends a fixed token budget (default 1k) on the most-referenced symbols, personalised by what is in chat; (2) treating code editing as a text-format problem instead of tool calling, with per-model edit formats (diff, udiff, whole, patch, editor-*), permissive application (whitespace-tolerant, `...` wildcards, SequenceMatcher fuzzy match at 0.8), and a benchmark metric for format compliance, which is why it could run on any chat model years before structured tool use was universal; (3) the architect/editor split that lets a reasoning model plan while a cheaper model formats edits, plus git-as-safety-net where every AI edit is its own attributed commit. The loudest criticisms in 2026: it is interactive-only with no agent loop, tools, MCP, hooks, or sub-agents ('Aider waits on each prompt', 'needs a human at the keyboard', Tembo 2026-05-06; 'doesn't orchestrate across 40 files and coordinate sub-agents', jock.pl 2026-04-15); and it is barely maintained (no tagged release since Aug 2025, one PyPI patch Feb 2026, ~500 open PRs and ~1.4k+ issues, the 'Where is Paul?' issue #4613 of 2025-10-30 and the 2026-01-07 direction question #4751 both unanswered; HN users call it 'in a sad state'), with the cecli/aider-ce fork shipping weekly to fill the gap.

unknowns: hooks: no lifecycle hook/event system is documented anywhere in the docs, options reference, or base_coder.py; described by absence
subagents: no sub-agent facility documented; only the architect/editor and weak-model roles exist
mcp: no native MCP/ACP/A2A support documented; only open issues and third-party wrappers
permissions: no permission modes or sandbox documented; only per-action confirm prompts and --yes-always
tools: no documented truncation limit for shell/lint/test output fed back to the model

identity: exact first release date (v0.5.0 on 2023-06-08 is the oldest visible on PyPI; earlier tags may have existed); PyPI download figures beyond the README's own 6.8M claim were not independently verified
loop: whether the main-branch model additions (Claude 4.5/4.6, GPT-5.x, Gemini 3) have shipped in any tagged release after v0.86.2 could not be confirmed

profiles.name: Cline and Roo Code (cline/cline; RooCodeInc/Roo-Code, archived 2026-05-15)
profiles.one_liner: Cline is the 69k-star Apache-2.0 TypeScript coding agent that grew from a VS Code extension into an SDK/CLI/desktop runtime with Plan/Act, shadow-git checkpoints, hooks, plugins and sub-agents; Roo Code was its most successful fork (custom modes, Orchestrator/Boomerang sub-tasks, allow/deny command lists), which shipped its final release v3.54.0 and archived the repo on 2026-05-15 when the team pivoted to the Roomote cloud agent, leaving the community fork Zoo Code and Cline as the recommended successors.

dimensions.identity: Cline: maintained by Cline Bot Inc. (founder Saoud Rizwan); built June 2024 for an Anthropic hackathon as "Claude Dev", published to the VS Code Marketplace July 2024, renamed Cline ("CLI aNd Editor") with v2.0 in October 2024; Apache-2.0, TypeScript; $32M raised by July 2025. Distribution in Sept 2026: VS Code extension (v4.1.21, 2026-09-24), JetBrains plugin, CLI (`npm install -g cline`, CLI v3.0.65), Desktop app (macOS/Windows, Linux .deb/.rpm since Desktop v0.0.35; v0.0.37 on 2026-09-26), Node SDK (`@cline/sdk` v0.0.86), Kanban board (`npx kanban`); README shows 69.4k stars, the SDK blog (2026-05-13) claims "over 7m developers", secondaries cite 4M+ installs by May 2026. Roo Code: Roo Code, Inc. (CEO Matt Rubens; marketplace publisher "Roo Veterinary Inc", id `RooVeterinaryInc.roo-cline`); forked from Cline in late 2024 as "Roo Cline" after Cline declined a multi-mode/per-project-instructions design (HN, Feb 2025), renamed Roo Code early 2025; Apache-2.0, TypeScript; VS Code extension plus a `roo` CLI (macOS arm64 / Linux x64, Node 20+); 24.3k stars, 3.4k forks, ~2.0M installs on the marketplace page (secondaries say 3M). Status: sunset announced ~2026-04-20/22, last team release v3.53.0 on 2026-04-23, final automated release v3.54.0 and repo archive on 2026-05-15; Roo Code Cloud and Router are offline; the marketplace listing now says the extension "was shut down on May 15th" and points to ZooCode (`ZooCodeOrganization.zoo-code`, v3.54.0 published 2026-05-16, continuing from 3.53.0) and Cline. The team's successor product is Roomote (github.com/RooCodeInc/Roomote, Fair Core License FCL-1.0-ALv2, self-hosted via Docker Compose, free up to 10 users, 260 stars).
dimensions.loop: Cline: a single ReAct-style tool loop; the SDK's `@cline/agents` `Agent` exposes `run(input)`, `continue()`, `abort()`, `subscribe()`, `restore(messages)`, `snapshot()` and emits `iteration_start`/`iteration_end`/`usage`/`done` events, with `AgentRunResult.status` in {completed, aborted, failed}. A run ends when a tool marked `lifecycle: { completesRun: true }` executes (the built-in `submit_and_exit`; legacy XML name `attempt_completion`), on abort, or on failure; tool errors are returned as `{ output: { error }, isError: true }` so they do not increment the "mistake counter" (its limit is not documented, nor is a max-iteration cap; CLI `--timeout <seconds>` defaults to none). Plan/Act wraps the loop: Plan mode can read, search and discuss but cannot edit or run commands, conversation history carries over on switch, different models can be assigned per mode ("Use different models for Plan and Act"), and model-driven mode switching was removed in favour of user control; `/deep-planning` runs silent investigation -> questions -> `implementation_plan.md` -> a fresh task with trackable steps, and Focus Chain keeps a persistent todo list that Cline re-reads every 6 messages. Roo Code: the same single loop (inherited), where a turn ends with `attempt_completion` or pauses on `ask_followup_question` (auto-answer timeout 1-300s when auto-approved); the loop is wrapped by a mode (role prompt + tool groups) and by Orchestrator mode, which delegates via `new_task(mode, message)` into a child with a fresh context whose `attempt_completion.result` is the only thing returned. Loop guards: the "Error & Repetition Limit" (`consecutiveMistakeLimit`, since v3.23; 0 disables; CLI `--consecutive-mistake-limit` default 10) plus a tool-repetition detector; native tool protocol became the default in v3.36.13 and parallel tool execution was experimental from v3.34.5.
dimensions.tools: Cline (SDK era): a tool is `createTool({ name, description, inputSchema (zod or JSON Schema), async execute(input, context) })`, registered via `extraTools` in ClineCore config, the `tools` array of `Agent`, or `api.registerTool()` inside a plugin; `execute` returns JSON, errors as `{ output: { error }, isError: true }`, and long tools should honour `context.signal`. Built-ins listed on the SDK tools page: `read_files`, `search_codebase`, `run_commands`, `fetch_web_content`, `apply_patch`, `editor`, `skills`, `ask_question`, `submit_and_exit` (the tools-reference page names them `bash`, `editor`, `read_files`, `apply_patch`, `search`, `fetch_web`, `ask_question`; the legacy XML names were `read_file`, `replace_in_file`, `execute_command`), plus `use_subagents`, `use_skill`, `team_*` and MCP tools; `Agent` from `@cline/agents` ships with no built-ins. Native (JSON) tool calling has been default since v3.35 (Nov 2025) for Claude 4+, Gemini 2.5, GPT-5, Grok 4 families, cutting prompt size ~15% and enabling parallel tool calls, with XML fallback for other models. Truncation is hard-coded (issue #13263, Aug 2026, open): 2,000 lines per `read_files` call, ~48k-char per-read budget, ~48k chars for `search_codebase` and `run_commands`, 8k chars for generic tool results, 50k for file content and `fetch_web_content`. Roo Code: tools are defined inside the extension and grouped for mode permissions (read, edit, browser, command, mcp, modes, workflow): `read_file`, `list_files`, `read_command_output`, `search_files`, `codebase_search`, `apply_diff`, `apply_patch`, `edit`, `edit_file`, `search_replace`, `write_to_file`, `generate_image`, `execute_command`, `run_slash_command`, `use_mcp_tool`, `access_mcp_resource`, `update_todo_list`, `skill`, and the four always-available `ask_followup_question`, `attempt_completion`, `switch_mode`, `new_task`; v3.48 added a `disabledTools` admin setting and removed the browser tool. `read_file` takes `offset`/`limit` (default 2,000 lines) or multi-file `line_range`, auto-truncates above `maxReadFileLine` (UI default 500; 0 = definitions only), reads up to 5 files concurrently (1-100), and emits "Showing lines ... of N" notices; `execute_command` output is captured via VS Code shell integration, throttled every 100 ms, and overflow is fetched with `read_command_output`.
dimensions.extensibility: Cline: the SDK plugin model is the main surface. A plugin is an `AgentPlugin` object `{ name, manifest: { capabilities: ["tools","hooks"] }, setup(api, ctx), hooks }`, declared in `package.json` under `cline.plugins[]` (`paths`, `capabilities`), installed with `cline plugin install <source>` (raw URL, git repo `@ref`, `npm:@scope/name`, local path) into `~/.cline/plugins/_installed/` or project `.cline/plugins/`, or passed as `extensions: [plugin]` / `pluginPaths` in session config; plugins can register tools, lifecycle hooks, slash commands and rules, and the reference example is `cline/typescript-lsp-plugin` adding a `goto_definition` tool. Providers are pluggable by implementing an `ApiHandler` and registering it in the `@cline/llms` registry (catalog: 6,386 models across 209 providers as of 4.1.21). Prompt-level extension: rules in `.clinerules/` or `.cline/rules/` (plus `AGENTS.md`, `.cursorrules`, `.windsurfrules`, global `~/Documents/Cline/Rules`) with YAML `paths:` frontmatter for conditional rules; skills as `SKILL.md` in `.cline/skills/`, `.clinerules/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `~/.cline/skills/` with progressive loading (~100 tokens metadata, <5k on trigger) and a Customize marketplace; workflows/slash commands; MCP servers; messaging connectors (`cline connect`) and cron `cline schedule`. Roo Code: extensibility was mode-centric rather than code-centric. Custom modes live in `.roomodes` (project) or `custom_modes.yaml` (global) with `slug`, `name`, `roleDefinition`, `whenToUse`, `description`, `customInstructions`, `groups` (with `fileRegex` edit restrictions), sticky per-mode model, import/export and project-over-global precedence; rules in `.roo/rules/`, `.roo/rules-{modeSlug}/`, `.roorules`, `AGENTS.md` (`roo-cline.useAgentRules`), global `~/.roo/rules/`; skills per the agentskills.io spec in `.roo/skills/`, `.agents/skills/`, `skills-{mode}/`; slash commands (v3.38 added an optional `mode` field); MCP; and an in-extension Marketplace of MCPs and Modes writing to `.roo/mcp.json`/`.roomodes` or global files. There was no plugin API or hook API, the file-based system-prompt override was removed in 3.48, and new providers required a PR to the extension.
dimensions.context: Cline: Auto Compact summarises the conversation when it nears the model's context limit, preserving decisions, file changes and project context, and replaces history with the summary; it "leverages your existing prompt cache" so it costs about one tool call, checkpoints let you restore to before the summary, and for non-Claude models it falls back to rule-based truncation (trigger threshold is not documented); `/smol` compacts manually. Focus Chain todo lists are re-read every 6 messages to survive compaction, `/deep-planning` hands off into a fresh task with `implementation_plan.md`, conditional rules load only when `paths:` globs match, and skills load progressively. Memory Bank is a documented prompt convention, not a mechanism: a `.clinerules/memory-bank.md` rule drives six files (`projectbrief.md`, `productContext.md`, `activeContext.md`, `systemPatterns.md`, `techContext.md`, `progress.md`) via "initialize/update memory bank" phrases. For local models the docs require "Use Compact Prompt", and 4.1.21 added output-token recovery with compact-and-retry for local models; native tool calling reduces prompt tokens ~15%. Roo Code: Intelligent Context Condensing uses an LLM to summarise earlier messages when usage crosses a slider threshold (default 100%, per-profile overrides), with a manual "Condense Context" button and a customisable condensing prompt; slash commands in the first message survive condensation, and the older sliding-window truncation remains the fallback. Codebase Indexing chunks code with Tree-sitter (100-1,000 chars, 1MB/file, `.gitignore`/`.rooignore` respected), embeds via OpenAI/Gemini/Ollama/Mistral/Bedrock/OpenRouter/OpenAI-compatible, stores in Qdrant, and exposes `codebase_search` (score threshold default 0.4); smart code folding keeps ~50k chars of file signatures. Persistent memory: `AGENTS.md` and rules directories; `update_todo_list`; Roo Code Cloud task sync (now offline). KV-cache/prompt-caching behaviour is not documented for either beyond Cline's Auto Compact note.
dimensions.permissions: Cline: the auto-approve panel has paired toggles: Read project files / Read all files (outside workspace), Edit project files / Edit all files, Execute safe commands / Execute all commands, Use the browser, Use MCP servers, plus notifications for commands over 30 s. "Safe" is not an allowlist: "the model marks each command with a `requires_approval` flag" (e.g. `npm test`, `git status` safe; `npm install`, `rm -rf`, `sed -i` not). YOLO mode (v3.31) auto-approves everything including Plan->Act; enterprises can lock it with `"yoloModeAllowed": false` in remote config, and MCP servers carry per-tool `autoApprove` arrays. In the SDK, `toolPolicies` are `{ autoApprove: true|false }` or `{ enabled: false }` (unlisted tools default to enabled and auto-approved) plus a `requestToolApproval(request) -> { approved }` capability callback; the CLI's `--auto-approve` defaults to true and `-y` is headless. Env-level fences: `CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS` (JSON allow/deny shell-command policy), `CLINE_SANDBOX` (isolated data dir), `.clineignore` (being deprecated). There is no OS sandbox or container; isolation comes from git worktrees (Kanban), SSH remotes (Desktop) and hooks that can veto. Roo Code: a master auto-approve switch (Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+A) over categories: read files (+ outside workspace), edit files (+ outside workspace, + protected files, with a write delay tied to VS Code diagnostics), execute approved commands with allowlist/denylist prefix matching (longest prefix wins, deny wins ties, commands using parameter/process substitution are blocked even if allowed), browser, MCP (global toggle AND per-tool `alwaysAllow`), switch modes, create/complete subtasks, auto-answer follow-ups (1-300 s), retry API. Modes add a structural fence via `groups` and `fileRegex` (Orchestrator cannot read, write, run or call MCP at all), `.rooignore` blocks reads, `disabledTools` removes tools; the `roo` CLI auto-approves by default unless `--require-approval`. The docs warn auto-approve "can result in data loss, file corruption, or worse"; no sandbox or container isolation existed.
dimensions.hooks: Cline has two hook systems. Script hooks (v3.36, 2025-11-06): executables named exactly after the event in `~/Documents/Cline/Rules/Hooks/` or `.clinerules/hooks/`, receiving JSON on stdin and returning `{ "cancel": bool, "contextModification": string }`, for events PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserPromptSubmit, TaskStart, TaskResume, TaskCancel; macOS/Linux only at launch; `cancel: true` vetoes and `contextModification` injects text into the conversation. SDK plugin hooks (2026): a plugin's `hooks` object may implement `beforeRun`, `afterRun`, `beforeModel`, `afterModel`, `beforeTool`, `afterTool`, `onEvent` (runtime stages `run_start`, `run_end`, `tool_call_before`, `tool_call_after`, `error`); the June 2026 blog shows `beforeTool` returning `{ skip: true, reason }` to block a call, i.e. hooks can veto, although the writing-plugins page still describes hooks as "for observation ... not for modifying agent behavior". Extra hook directories come from `--hooks-dir` / `CLINE_HOOKS_DIR`. Roo Code: not documented; there was no lifecycle-hook system. The closest request, issue #11504 "[ENHANCEMENT] Allow prompt based hook" (2026-02-17) asking for pre/post-tool-use hooks like Claude Code's, was still open and unanswered when the repo was archived.
dimensions.subagents: Cline: the `use_subagents` tool (enabled by default across VS Code, JetBrains, CLI) launches parallel read-only research agents, each with its own prompt, context window and token budget; they may only use `read_file`, `list_files`, `search_files`, `list_code_definition_names`, read-only `execute_command` and `use_skill`, cannot edit, browse, call MCP or spawn nested subagents, inherit the "Read project files" auto-approve setting, and return a report of the most relevant file paths with per-agent tool-call/token/cost stats rolled into the task. The SDK adds `enableSpawnAgent` and Agent Teams (`enableAgentTeams: true`, `teamName`; CLI `cline --team-name auth-sprint "..."`, `/team`, `--no-teams`; SDK/CLI/Kanban only): a coordinator gets `team_spawn_teammate`, `team_delegate_task`, `team_check_status`, `team_get_result`; teammates inherit the coordinator's `providerId`, `modelId` and credentials with role-specific prompts; state persists in `~/.cline/data/teams/<name>/{task-board.json, mailbox.json, mission-log.json}` across sessions; no team-size or depth limit is documented. Kanban runs one agent per card in its own git worktree, and the hub-spoke runtime (hub daemon at `127.0.0.1:25463`, WebSocket clients as creator/participant/observer) lets several clients share one session. Roo Code: Orchestrator (Boomerang) mode spawns subtasks with `new_task(mode, message)`; each child "operates in complete isolation with its own conversation history", receives only what the message says, runs in its own mode (so a cheap model can be assigned per mode), and returns only its `attempt_completion` `result` to the parent, which then resumes automatically ("metadata-driven subtasks with automatic parent resume and single-open safety", v3.35.0); 3.48 added a recursive subtask history tree. Auto-approve has a "Create & complete subtasks" toggle; depth and budget limits are not documented. Roo Code Cloud agents existed but were shut down with the product.
dimensions.providers: Cline: `@cline/llms` is the provider layer (handlers, gateway creation, model catalogs, runtime registry); a new provider is an `ApiHandler` plus registration, and 4.1.21 refreshed the catalog to 6,386 models across 209 providers. First-party paths include the Cline provider (usage billing, ClinePass, free models such as MiniMax M2.5 and Kimi K2.5 in CLI 2.0) and an OpenAI-compatible Cline API; documented providers include Anthropic (incl. Claude Code), OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, Vertex, OpenRouter, Cerebras, Groq, DeepSeek, Qwen, Z.AI, MiniMax, Poolside, LiteLLM and generic OpenAI-compatible endpoints (which is how vLLM/llama.cpp are reached). Local runtimes: Ollama (`http://localhost:11434`), LM Studio (`http://localhost:1234`), Atomic Chat, with RAM tiers (16-32 GB small quantised, 32-64 GB mid, 64 GB+ large); weak/local models get the mandatory "Use Compact Prompt", XML tool-calling fallback for models without native tool support, and (4.1.21) output-token recovery with compaction retry. Cline publishes open-weight Terminal-Bench 2.0 runs (Kimi K2.6 55.1%, DeepSeek V4 Pro 53.9%, GLM-5.1 49.4% under Cline CLI). Roo Code: 50+ providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, Vertex, OpenRouter, xAI, Mistral, Groq, Poe, Vercel AI Gateway, Ollama, LM Studio, OpenAI-compatible) plus the Roo Code Router (renamed from "Cloud Provider" in 3.39.3, now offline); nine low-usage providers were dropped in 3.48. The Ollama page auto-detects `num_ctx`, recommends 16384/32768/65536 for ~8/16/24+ GB VRAM, uses `qwen2.5-coder:32b` as its example and warns about cold-start OOM; weak models are handled by per-mode model assignment, the consecutive-mistake/repetition limit, and a grace retry for "no tools used" (PR #10196).
dimensions.mcp: Cline: MCP client with stdio, Streamable HTTP (recommended) and legacy SSE transports; config in `~/.cline/data/settings/cline_mcp_settings.json` (IDE) or `~/.cline/mcp.json` (CLI), managed via the MCP Servers panel, a Remote Servers tab or `cline mcp`; per-server `autoApprove` arrays, enable/disable/restart, request timeouts; an MCP marketplace, streamable servers and pre-registered OAuth clients per the changelog; enterprise remote config has MCP Server Controls. Beyond MCP, Cline speaks the Agent Client Protocol: `cline --acp` serves Zed, JetBrains AI Assistant, Neovim (CodeCompanion/avante), Emacs and other ACP clients with Plan/Act switching, model selection, approvals and session restore; the CLI also has messaging connectors (`cline connect` for Slack/Telegram/Discord) and OpenTelemetry export for enterprise. A2A is not documented. Roo Code: MCP client with global `mcp_settings.json` and project `.roo/mcp.json` (project wins on name clash); stdio entries take `command`, `args` (with `${env:VAR}`), `cwd`, `env`, `alwaysAllow`, `disabled`, `timeout` (1-3600 s, default 60), `watchPaths`, `disabledTools`; remote entries use `type: "streamable-http"` or `"sse"` with `url` and `headers`; wildcard config arrived in 3.44; an "MCP Server Creation" mode lets Roo scaffold servers; the in-extension Marketplace installs MCPs and Modes; tools are called via `use_mcp_tool` / `access_mcp_resource`. ACP and A2A are not documented for Roo Code.
dimensions.evals: Cline: (1) cline-bench (announced 2025-11-17 with a $1M sponsorship pool) turns real Cline user sessions on open-source repos into Harbor-format containerised tasks (`instruction.md`, `task.toml`, `environment/Dockerfile`, `solution/solve.sh`, `tests/` with binary 0/1 reward), runnable on local Docker or Daytona; it is "early access" with no leaderboard yet. (2) Terminal-Bench 2.0: the SDK launch post (2026-05-13) reports Cline CLI at 74.2% with claude-opus-4.7 versus Anthropic's published 69.4% for Claude Code on the same model, plus open-weight rows (Kimi K2.6 55.1%, DeepSeek V4 Pro 53.9%, GLM-5.1 49.4%); the `cline/benchmark-results` repo publishes a June 24-25, 2026 harness-vs-harness run (Cline CLI 3.0.29 vs OpenCode 1.17.9 vs Pi-Code 0.73.1, 89 tasks, pass@1, timeout x2, n=20, OpenRouter+Modal) which is the closest thing to a harness ablation, with the caveat that the OpenCode/Pi-Code numbers are not those projects' official runs. No SWE-bench results are published. Roo Code: an in-repo evals system (`packages/evals`, web dashboard on port 3446) ran Exercism exercises (Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, Rust; methodology credited to Aider) from the `RooCodeInc/Roo-Code-Evals` repo in Docker runners (`debian:bookworm-slim` with VS Code and the extension), headless-VS Code or CLI execution, Postgres for run/task/metrics/tool-error storage and Redis for heartbeats, recommended 3 GB x concurrency; it recorded pass/fail, tokens, cost, duration and tool errors and once fed a public results page. No SWE-bench/Terminal-Bench numbers or harness-vs-model ablations were published, and the results site is offline since the shutdown.
dimensions.distinctive: Cline's distinctive ideas: (1) the hub-spoke runtime (singleton hub daemon at `127.0.0.1:25463` brokering sessions, approvals and schedules; spokes run the loop; CLI, VS Code, JetBrains and desktop attach over WebSocket with "capability brokerage" so one session can use VS Code for file ops and the CLI for shell), with sessions persisted in `~/.cline/data/sessions/` (SQLite index + JSON) independent of any UI; (2) Plan/Act as a first-class human-in-the-loop primitive, combined with model-classified `requires_approval` instead of a command allowlist; (3) shadow-git checkpoints after every tool use with three restore modes, later extended into cline-bench (real failed sessions become RL environments). Loudest criticisms: Mindgard's disclosure (Nov 2025; GHSA-3c6h-5gc7-73gj DNS exfiltration via an auto-approved "safe" `ping`, GHSA-vgj6-8c6w-xw63 `.clinerules` prompt injection forcing `requires_approval=false`, GHSA-pvpq-899w-5mqr TOCTOU) and the slow vendor response, which is exactly the cost of model-judged safety; hard-coded truncation limits (#13263); CLI `--auto-approve` defaulting to true; checkpoints slowing large repos; and post-SDK doc drift (tool names differ across pages, the hooks page is a stub). Roo Code's distinctive ideas: (1) the custom mode as the unit of configuration (role prompt + tool groups + `fileRegex` + sticky model, shareable via `.roomodes` and the Marketplace); (2) Orchestrator/Boomerang sub-tasks with fresh contexts returning only an `attempt_completion` summary, explicitly justified as preventing "context poisoning", plus cheap-model-per-mode cost splitting; (3) deterministic command gating (allow/deny prefix lists, longest-prefix-wins, deny on tie, substitution guard) and Qdrant codebase indexing. Loudest criticisms: the shutdown itself (announced April 2026, archived 2026-05-15; secondaries quote that "free open-source extensions do not pay for the team's salaries", and the 3.54 marketplace notice now redirects users to ZooCode/Cline); a fast, experimental cadence (16 point releases of 3.36 in two weeks) and breaking removals (browser tool, system-prompt override); orchestrator fan-out cost; weak context summarisation (secondary); and no hooks or plugin API.

unknowns: Roo Cline's exact first-release date on the VS Code Marketplace: only 'late 2024' from secondary sources and the Feb 2025 HN thread; the changelog fetch was truncated before the 2.x entries and the docs' v2.1.2 page shows a build date, not a release date.
Cline Auto Compact trigger threshold (percentage/tokens) and the mistake-counter limit / any max-iteration cap in the SDK loop: not documented on the pages read.
Cline Focus Chain's '6 messages' interval comes from a Cline Threads post surfaced in search, not from a docs page (the docs/features/focus-chain URL was not found).
Exact JSON schema of CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS (allow/deny/allowRedirects): the primary config page names the variable but the field example came only from secondary search snippets.
Roo Code lifecycle hooks: none existed; only an open enhancement issue (#11504). Listed as 'not documented'.
Roo Code orchestrator nesting depth and per-subtask budget limits: not documented.
KV-cache / prompt-caching behaviour for both projects beyond Cline's Auto Compact note: not documented on the pages read.

Roo Code's public evals results page and per-model pass rates: offline after the shutdown; packages/evals/ARCHITECTURE.md returned 404, so infrastructure details rely on the Roo-Code-Evals README plus a DeepWiki secondary.
The per-model results table of Cline's June 2026 Terminal-Bench open-weights harness comparison (summary.md/summary.csv) was not read; only the methodology README.

profiles.name: OpenHands (OpenHands/OpenHands, formerly All-Hands-AI/OpenHands, formerly OpenDevin)
profiles.one_liner: MIT-licensed, model-agnostic coding-agent platform whose 2026 shape is a Python "Software Agent SDK" (event-sourced loop, typed Pydantic tools, optional Docker/K8s agent-server, inline LLM risk labeling) fronted by a TypeScript "Agent Canvas" control center that can also drive Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI over ACP.

dimensions.identity: Maintained by the OpenHands GitHub org (the company All Hands AI, founded by Robert Brennan, Xingyao Wang and Graham Neubig; USD 5M seed from Menlo Ventures, Sep 2024); the org was renamed from All-Hands-AI to OpenHands around Oct 20, 2025 and images moved from ghcr.io/all-hands-ai/ to ghcr.io/openhands/. First released as OpenDevin on March 12, 2024, renamed OpenHands in August 2024; core is MIT, enterprise components are proprietary. Since June 1, 2026 the flagship repo OpenHands/OpenHands holds 'Agent Canvas' (React/TypeScript on Node.js 24; `docker run ... ghcr.io/openhands/agent-canvas:1.24.0` or `npm install -g @openhands/agent-canvas`, plus macOS DMG and Linux desktop installers), while the harness proper is the Python SDK (`pip install openhands-sdk openhands-tools`, v1.49.6 released Sep 25, 2026, Python >=3.12); the old Python app was moved to the archived OpenHands/legacy repo and the CLI (`uv tool install openhands --python 3.12`, settings in ~/.openhands/settings.json) is labelled 'feature-complete and primarily maintained for stability'. Popularity: 89,187 stars / 11,747 forks on the main repo and 1,171 stars on software-agent-sdk as of Sep 26, 2026; the June 2026 launch post cites 77,000+ stars and 'millions of downloads'. A commercial OpenHands Cloud and Enterprise offering sit alongside the open-source pieces.
dimensions.loop: V1 is a single ReAct-style function-calling loop (the V0 'CodeAct' Python-as-action paradigm no longer exists in the SDK): `Agent.step()` first executes any actions that were waiting for confirmation, then runs the condenser, calls the LLM, parses the response into ActionEvents or a MessageEvent, holds actions at the confirmation gate, executes tools and appends ObservationEvents. A turn ends when the model returns a plain text message with no tool calls or calls the built-in `finish` tool (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/tool/builtins/finish.py); `Conversation.run()` then returns, and the conversation status moves through IDLE, RUNNING, PAUSED, WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION, FINISHED, ERROR, STUCK, DELETING (FINISHED/ERROR/STUCK are terminal). `Conversation(..., max_iteration_per_run=500)` is the step cap (source: openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/conversation.py) and `stuck_detection=True` by default trips on the same action-observation 4+ times, same action-error 3+ times, 3+ consecutive agent messages without progress, a 6-cycle alternating pattern, or repeated context-window errors. State is event-sourced: an append-only EventLog persisted as base_state.json plus one JSON file per event, with resume by replay; `tool_concurrency_limit` (default 1) lets the SDK execute several tool calls from one LLM response in parallel.
dimensions.tools: A tool is four Pydantic pieces: an `Action` (input schema), an `Observation` (with a `to_llm_content` property that decides what the model sees), a `ToolExecutor[Action, Observation]` with `__call__`, and a `ToolDefinition.create()` that ties them together; you register with `register_tool("GrepTool", GrepTool)` (instance, subclass or factory) and hand the agent `Agent(llm=llm, tools=[Tool(name="GrepTool")])`. Each definition carries MCP-style `ToolAnnotations` (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint); the terminal tool is annotated readOnlyHint=False, destructiveHint=True, openWorldHint=True. The openhands-tools package ships terminal (tmux/subprocess/PowerShell backends, `is_input` for interactive processes, `reset`), file_editor, task_tracker, browser_use (BrowserToolSet), grep, glob, apply_patch (GPT-5 preset), task (TaskToolSet), delegate, ask_oracle, tom_consult, planning_file_editor and workflow, plus SDK built-ins `finish` and `think`; `get_default_tools(enable_browser=True, enable_sub_agents=False)` gives Terminal + FileEditor + TaskTracker (+Browser). Output is truncated by `maybe_truncate()` (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/utils/truncate.py), which keeps head and tail and can persist the full text to a file; the terminal uses `MAX_CMD_OUTPUT_SIZE = 30000` characters (openhands-tools/openhands/tools/terminal/constants.py) and the generic `DEFAULT_TEXT_CONTENT_LIMIT = 50_000`.
dimensions.extensibility: Almost every component is a typed, immutable Pydantic object you can subclass and swap: tools via `register_tool`, agents via `register_agent` factories or `ACPAgent`, LLMs via LiteLLM model strings and `Router` subclasses (`MultimodalRouter` ships), condensers via `CondenserBase`/`RollingCondenser`, analyzers via `SecurityAnalyzerBase`, confirmation policies, visualizers and workspaces. Prompt-level extension uses Skills: `Skill(name, content, trigger=KeywordTrigger|PathTrigger|None)` in `AgentContext`, loaded from AGENTS.md/.cursorrules (always in the system prompt), `.agents/skills/` SKILL.md folders (AgentSkills standard, progressive disclosure via `<available_skills>`), `.openhands/skills/installed/` and `~/.openhands/skills/`. Plugins bundle skills, `hooks/hooks.json`, `agents/*.md`, `commands/*.md` and `.mcp.json` under a `.plugin/plugin.json` manifest in a layout the docs call compatible with Claude Code plugins; `Plugin.load(path)`, `PluginSource("github:owner/repo")`, `conversation.load_plugin("name@marketplace")` and `~/.openhands/plugins/installed/` with `.installed.json` handle loading and persistence. Third parties publish to the OpenHands/extensions registry (64 skills, 10 plugins as of Sep 2026) by adding `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and an entry in `marketplaces/openhands-extensions.json`; `AgentContext(load_public_skills=True)` clones it to `~/.openhands/cache/skills/`. On the UI side, Agent Canvas adds pluggable backends (local, Docker, remote VM, Modal, Kubernetes/Helm, Cloud), ACP agent presets and a 'Canvas Extensions / Apps (Beta)' frontend extension point (v1.16.0).
dimensions.context: Compaction is a condenser attached to the agent: `LLMSummarizingCondenser(llm=..., max_size=240, keep_first=2)` are the source defaults (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/context/condenser/llm_summarizing_condenser.py; the docs page still says 120), and when the event count exceeds `max_size` it emits a `Condensation` event holding `forgotten_event_ids`, a summary and `summary_offset`, which `View.from_events()` applies on the next step while the raw event log stays intact; `NoOpCondenser` and `PipelineCondenser` also exist, and the SDK paper claims up to 2x API-cost reduction with no measured accuracy loss. Memory files: AGENTS.md and .cursorrules are loaded as always-on repo skills, SKILL.md skills are disclosed on demand, and opt-in persistent memory (`AgentContext(load_memory=True)`) injects `~/.openhands/memory/MEMORY.md` and `<workspace>/.openhands/memory/MEMORY.md` as a `<MEMORY_CONTEXT>` block capped at about 6,000 characters, with dated `YYYY-MM-DD.md` logs the agent reads with its ordinary file tools. KV-cache friendliness: `LLM._apply_prompt_caching()` adds `cache_control: {type: ephemeral}` markers (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/llm/message.py) and `keep_first` preserves a stable prefix, but the docs do not discuss cache design explicitly. The local-LLM guide requires at least 22,000 tokens of context (recommends `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768`) because the system prompt alone overflows Ollama's 4,096 default.
dimensions.permissions: Gating is a confirmation policy plus a security analyzer on the Conversation: `conversation.set_confirmation_policy(NeverConfirm() | AlwaysConfirm() | ConfirmRisky(threshold=SecurityRisk.HIGH, confirm_unknown=...))`, with `NeverConfirm()` the default in ConversationState (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/state.py). `LLMSecurityAnalyzer` injects a required `security_risk` argument into every tool schema so the model labels each call LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/UNKNOWN inline at zero extra LLM calls; `PatternSecurityAnalyzer` (regex), `PolicyRailSecurityAnalyzer` (deterministic rules) and `EnsembleSecurityAnalyzer` (takes the max) are alternatives, and a gated action parks the conversation in WAITING_FOR_CONFIRMATION until `conversation.run()` (approve) or `conversation.reject_pending_actions(reason)` (deny, feedback goes back to the model). Sandboxing is 'optional isolation': `LocalWorkspace` runs tools in-process with no fence, `DockerWorkspace(server_image="ghcr.io/openhands/agent-server:latest-python", host_port=8010, mount=..., forward_env=...)` runs the whole agent-server in a container (VSCode at host_port+1, VNC at +2), and Apptainer, RemoteAPIWorkspace, Kubernetes `AgentSandboxWorkspace` (SDK v1.48.0) and OpenHands Cloud are further options; the docs state the process sandbox (`RUNTIME=process`) 'provides no sandbox isolation'. Agent Canvas adds per-conversation execution isolation (`OH_EXECUTION_RUNTIME=docker`, `OH_EXECUTION_IMAGE`, `OH_EXECUTION_VOLUMES`) that runs only terminal/file_editor/grep/glob/apply_patch in an ephemeral container at /workspace while the loop, credentials and LLM calls stay on the host. Caveat: for ACP-driven agents 'permission requests from the server are automatically granted, so ensure you trust the ACP server'.
dimensions.hooks: The SDK ships a `HookConfig` with six lifecycle events: PreToolUse (blocking), PostToolUse (non-blocking), UserPromptSubmit (blocking), Stop (blocking, fires when the agent tries to finish), SessionStart and SessionEnd (non-blocking), attached via `Conversation(agent, hook_config=HookConfig(pre_tool_use=[HookMatcher(matcher="terminal", hooks=[HookDefinition(command="check.sh", timeout=10)])]))` or `HookConfig.from_dict()` which accepts the Claude Code `{"hooks": {"PreToolUse": [...]}}` layout. Hooks can veto: exit code 2 blocks the tool call, user message or completion, exit 0 allows and stdout is parsed as `{"decision": "allow"|"deny", "reason": ..., "additionalContext": ..., "continue": ...}`, and exit 1 is a logged non-blocking error; async hooks in PreToolUse cannot block. `HookType` is COMMAND (subprocess), PROMPT (one LLM completion) or AGENT (a sub-agent with tool access, copying the conversation's LLM), and hook spend is tracked and merged into the parent conversation's metrics. Below hooks, `Conversation(callbacks=[on_event])` and `token_callbacks` fire after each committed event, which is how the security analyzer, pause/resume and UI streaming interleave with the loop.
dimensions.subagents: Delegation is an ordinary tool: `TaskToolSet` (openhands-tools/openhands/tools/task/, off by default via `get_default_tools(enable_sub_agents=False)`) exposes `TaskAction(prompt, subagent_type="general-purpose", description, resume=<task_id>)`; child agents come from factories registered with `register_agent(name="animal_expert", factory_func=create_animal_expert)` that receive the parent's `LLM` and decide their own tools and `AgentContext` skills. A child runs as an independent Conversation in the parent's workspace, synchronously (the parent blocks) unless the orchestrator sets `tool_concurrency_limit` (the docs' example uses 8 to fan out to three sub-agents at once), and returns a `TaskObservation(task_id, subagent, status=completed|error, text)`; a `TaskManager(confirmation_handler=...)` routes a child's confirmation prompts back to the user. The SDK paper says sub-agents 'inherit the parent's model configuration and workspace context'; the older `max_turns` field is deprecated ('maximum iterations are now determined by the agent definition or parent conversation') and the agent-server's sub_agents_router carries a per-agent-definition `max_iteration_per_run`. No depth limit or token budget for children is documented. A lower-level `delegate` tool (`DelegateAction(ids, tasks)`) and the `ACPAgent` (delegating a whole conversation to Claude Code/Codex/Gemini over JSON-RPC) are the other multi-agent paths.
dimensions.providers: The `LLM` Pydantic model wraps LiteLLM (>=1.93, 100+ providers) with `model="provider/name"` (e.g. `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929`, `openai/gpt-4o`), `base_url`, `api_key: SecretStr`, `num_retries=5`, `max_output_tokens`, `reasoning_effort`, `extended_thinking_budget` and a `native_tool_calling` switch; it speaks both Chat Completions and the OpenAI Responses API (gpt-5* auto-routes) and captures Anthropic ThinkingBlocks and OpenAI reasoning items. Weak or non-function-calling models go through `NonNativeToolCallingMixin`, which renders tool schemas as prompt text and parses calls out of the completion. Local models use the `openai/` prefix plus a base URL: Ollama `http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1`, LM Studio `:1234/v1`, vLLM/SGLang `:8000/v1`, with `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768` required; the May 21, 2026 guide recommends Qwen3.6-35B-A3B first and warns 'some local models may struggle with reliable tool use'. Multi-model routing is via `Router` subclasses (`MultimodalRouter` sends text-only turns to a cheaper model), an LLM registry/profile store and a fallback strategy; an experimental `APIBasedCritic` (success_threshold 0.6, max_iterations 3) re-prompts the agent when a critic model scores the trajectory low. Through ACP, Agent Canvas can also bill against an existing Claude Max, Codex Pro or Gemini subscription because the spawned CLI authenticates itself.
dimensions.mcp: MCP client support is built on FastMCP (fastmcp>=3.2): `Agent(llm, tools, mcp_config={"mcpServers": {"fetch": {"command": "uvx", "args": ["mcp-server-fetch"]}, "Notion": {"url": "https://mcp.notion.com/mcp", "auth": "oauth"}}}, filter_tools_regex=...)`; each remote tool is wrapped as an `MCPToolDefinition`/`MCPToolExecutor` with lazily generated Pydantic action models and `MCPToolObservation` content blocks, plugins can contribute `.mcp.json`, and Agent Canvas adds per-profile MCP scoping (v1.19.0), remote-server testing (v1.22.0) and OAuth token refresh (SDK v1.49.6). ACP (Agent Client Protocol, JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio) is first-class in both directions: `ACPAgent(acp_command=["npx", "-y", "@agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp"])` lets the SDK drive Claude Code, Codex (`@zed-industries/codex-acp`), Gemini CLI (`--acp`) or any stdio ACP server (tools, mcp_config, condenser and critic then raise NotImplementedError because the remote agent owns them), and `openhands acp` exposes OpenHands itself to Zed, JetBrains, VS Code and Toad. A2A was requested in software-agent-sdk issue #1060 and closed 'not planned'. Whether the SDK can serve as an MCP server is not documented.
dimensions.evals: The SDK paper (arXiv 2511.03690, v1 Nov 5, 2025, v2 Apr 22, 2026) reports SWE-bench Verified 72.8% with Claude Sonnet 4.5, 68.8% GPT-5 (reasoning=high), 68.0% Claude Sonnet 4 and 65.2% Qwen3 Coder 480B, and GAIA validation 67.9 / 62.4 / 57.6 / 41.2 for the same models, plus a claim that V1 'substantially reduces system-attributable failures over V0 with negligible event-sourcing overhead' (the specific failure numbers were not extractable from the HTML). The OpenHands Index (Jan 29, 2026) scores models on SWE-Bench Verified, Commit0, SWE-Bench Multimodal, SWT-Bench and GAIA using the SDK as the fixed scaffold; the Feb 20, 2026 follow-up found agents exploiting `git log` to recover reference solutions on Commit0 and a `--depth 1` shallow-clone fix (OpenHands/benchmarks#422) dropped MiniMax M2.5 from 50.0% to 18.8% and GPT 5.2 Codex from 62.5% to 50.0%. The OpenHands/benchmarks repo currently supports SWE-Bench, SWE-Bench Pro, GAIA, Commit0, OpenAgentSafety and ProgramBench (no Terminal-Bench); the Jun 25, 2026 benchmarks post cites Epoch AI's finding that scaffold choice is worth 11-15 points for top models and says about 20% of commits to OpenHands are agent-authored. Third-party tracker tensorfeed.ai lists OpenHands + Claude Sonnet 4.6 at 65.8 on SWE-bench Verified and 30.1 on Terminal-Bench, which I could not verify against an official source. No published harness-versus-bare-model ablation exists beyond the condenser cost study.
dimensions.distinctive: Three ideas stand out. (1) Event sourcing as the harness backbone: every message, action, observation and even each condensation is an immutable event in an append-only log, persisted as base_state.json plus per-event JSON, so a conversation can be paused, forked, replayed and moved between an in-process LocalConversation and a Docker/K8s agent-server RemoteConversation with the same Agent object. (2) Zero-cost inline risk labeling: instead of a separate judge call, a required `security_risk` argument is injected into every tool schema and `ConfirmRisky` gates on the model's own label, cheap but trusting the model to rate its own actions. (3) The June 2026 pivot to a harness of harnesses: Agent Canvas plus `ACPAgent` turn OpenHands into a control plane that schedules Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI on any backend, riding those tools' subscriptions. Loudest criticisms: heavy infrastructure (Docker, Node 24 plus uv, Dockerized OpenHands cannot reach an LM Studio bound to 127.0.0.1), churn from the pivot (the Python app archived to OpenHands/legacy, CLI in maintenance, settings reset at 1.0), permissive defaults (`NeverConfirm()` and auto-approved ACP permission requests), the sandbox being optional rather than enforced, unpredictable cost and context fragmentation on long tasks, weak local models failing at tool calling, benchmark hygiene issues such as the Commit0 git-history leak, and docs that drift from the source (condenser `max_size` 120 in docs versus 240 in code).

unknowns: Exact V0-vs-V1 system-attributable failure rates from the SDK paper (only the qualitative claim was extractable)
Any depth limit or token budget for nested sub-agents (max_turns is deprecated; nothing replaces it in the docs)
Whether a filesystem/workspace path fence exists in LocalWorkspace (docs say only that the process sandbox has no isolation)
Whether the SDK or agent-server can act as an MCP server (only MCP client support is documented)
Official OpenHands numbers on Terminal-Bench and SWE-bench Pro (only a third-party tracker lists them)
Package download counts (only GitHub stars were available)
Retry/backoff specifics of the LLM layer beyond num_retries=5 and retry_min_wait
